content:
Is Amazon Prime Instant Video a viable alternative to Netflix?
I watch a lot of currently airing shows and not a lot of movies, so paying $8 a month for Netflix isn't ideal to me; it'll rarely get used. But I can get Prime for $40/year with my college e-mail address and the shipping benefits are worth that price alone. Is their instant video library comparable at all? I really know nothing about it and I find the layout of that part of the site completely unusable. I'm asking for a Roku and a Prime subscription for Christmas -- should I forget about Netflix altogether?

I'd like to be able to catch up on shows that I can't torrent easily (The West Wing, MASH, etc.) and also watch niche movies when I'm in the mood (The last movie I watched on Netflix was Safety Not Guaranteed).

Any insight? Thanks!

EDIT: I feel I wasn't clear enough, since I've gotten a lot of replies that don't quite address my concerns. I'm getting Prime. The shipping benefits are easily worth the cost, especially when it's 50% off. What I'm essentially asking is if Prime's Instant Video library is good enough that I (a user that would only rarely use PIV OR Netflix) can just eliminate Netflix from my considerations altogether. It appears the answer is "Yes, but to be clear, Netflix is better."

EDIT 2: Since this has come up quite a bit, let me try to make it clear. The free year of Amazon Student only gives you the shipping benefits of Amazon Prime, not the lending library or the instant video. The 50% off purchase of Prime through Amazon Student, however, is the exact same as regular Amazon Prime, just much, much cheaper.
